questions.prompt: Why is retracting force lower than extending force at the same pressure?
questions.answer: The rod reduces the effective piston area
options: The rod reduces the effective piston area
The cap end has no piston seal
Pressure cannot reach the rod end
questions.explanation: The rod reduces the effective piston area. The course explains: Calculating Force Calculating Force The pressure cannot be exerted over all the surfaces inside the rod end of the cylinder. The pressure only acts on the “donut” or annular area.

questions.prompt: What does Pascal’s law state about pressure in a confined fluid?
questions.answer: Pressure acts equally throughout and in all directions
options: Pressure acts equally throughout and in all directions
Pressure exists only at the inlet
Pressure decreases to zero at the outlet
questions.explanation: Pressure acts equally throughout and in all directions. The course explains: Pascal’s Law Pascal’s Law States that in a confined container the same pressure exists throughout the entire volume of the fluid and acts perpendicular to all internal surfaces. Fluid flowing in a pipe is not confined because the pipe is not closed on all sides.

questions.prompt: How does pneumatic leverage produce a larger output force?
questions.answer: Apply the same pressure to a larger output piston area
options: Apply the same pressure to a larger output piston area
questions.explanation: Apply the same pressure to a larger output piston area. The course explains: Pneumatic Leverage Example If a force of 10 lbs. is applied over a small piston with 1 square- inch area, a pressure of 10 psi is created in the confined fluid. In accordance with Pascal’s law, the same 10 psi acts on a larger 10 in. piston creating 100 lbs. on the larger piston. https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=aoMCRG4zM2s

questions.prompt: At constant temperature, what happens when the volume of a fixed amount of air decreases?
questions.explanation: Its absolute pressure increases. The course explains: Pressure Boyle’s Law The air compressor creates air pressure by reducing its volume. The formula used to calculate the exact effect a change in volume has on pressure is called Boyle’s law Created by Robert Boyle in 1662. Pressure is inversely proportional to volume.

questions.prompt: What causes air to flow between connected areas?
options: The size of the pressure gauge
questions.explanation: A pressure difference. The course explains: Air Flow and Resistance A characteristic of air is that a difference in pressure causes air flow to occur. Air flows from areas of high pressure to areas of low pressure until pressure is the same throughout.

questions.prompt: Which factors affect airflow through an opening in the slide example?
questions.answer: Temperature, pressure difference, and orifice size
options: Temperature, pressure difference, and orifice size
Rod color, gauge diameter, and hose label
Only the number of cylinder seals
questions.explanation: Temperature, pressure difference, and orifice size. The course explains: Air Flow and Resistance Example If two containers at different pressures are connected together the air will flow from the higher pressure container to the lower pressure when the valve is opened. Rate of flow depends on: Temperature Difference in pressure Size of orifice.
